from_quote: particularly Iluſtrated and explained by the Preſident Monteſquieu and Mr. •ocke
rationale: The paragraph names "Mr. •ocke" (the first letter is lost in the scan; it is read as Locke) with Montesquieu as the writers who explained the division of a government's powers into three branches. It names the writer, not a passage of his Second Treatise.

from_quote: For the houſe of repreſentatives, the rule adopted in the conſtitution, is perhaps the proper one
rationale: The paragraph speaks of "the rule adopted in the constitution" for the representation of the house of representatives, which is the apportionment rule of Article I, Section 2, Clause 3.

from_quote: The conſtitution perhaps ſuggeſts thoſe, with ſome exceptions that are proper; whether it would be ſafe to give it the abſolute controul of the fleet and army at all times
rationale: The paragraph asks whether the president should have "the absolute controul of the fleet and army at all times, in peace and war," which refers to the command of the army and navy in Article II, Section 2, Clause 1.
to_quote: shall be Commander in Chief of the Army and Navy of the United States

from_quote: the right of direct taxation and of excite through all the ſtates
rationale: The paragraph names "the right of direct taxation and of excise through all the states" as the one power in the constitution it objects to, which is the taxing power of Article I, Section 8, Clause 1.
to_quote: To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises

from_quote: the mode preſcribed for the election of the members
rationale: The paragraph approves "the mode prescribed for the election of the members" of the house of representatives "by the people," which is Article I, Section 2, Clause 1.
to_quote: chosen every second Year by the People of the several States

from_quote: The right of originating money bills, and of impeachment, have alſo been properly aſſigned
rationale: The paragraph says the right of originating money bills has been assigned to the house of representatives, as Article I, Section 7, Clause 1 provides.
to_quote: All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives

from_quote: The right of originating money bills, and of impeachment, have alſo been properly aſſigned
rationale: The paragraph says the right of impeachment has been assigned to the house of representatives, as Article I, Section 2, Clause 5 provides.

from_quote: This has been done with the members of the houſe of repreſentatives, but departed from with thoſe of the Senate
rationale: The paragraph objects that the senators, unlike the representatives, are appointed by the states in their legislative characters rather than by the people, which refers to Article I, Section 3, Clause 1.

from_quote: that theſe ſtates will give up their equal ſuffrage in the ſenate
rationale: The paragraph speaks of the states' "equal suffrage in the senate" and of senators appointed by the states, which refers to Article I, Section 3, Clause 1.
to_quote: each Senator shall have one Vote

from_quote: ten members from Virginia, eight from Maſſachuſetts or Pennſylvania in the houſe of repreſentatives
rationale: The paragraph gives the number of members in the house of representatives for Virginia, Massachusetts and Pennsylvania (ten, eight and eight), the numbers in Article I, Section 2, Clause 3.

from_quote: the right to orig•nate money bills
rationale: The paragraph speaks of the right to originate money bills in the house of representatives, as Article I, Section 7, Clause 1 provides. A letter of the word "originate" is lost in the scan.
to_quote: All Bills for raising Revenue shall originate in the House of Representatives

from_quote: By the conſent of two thirds of the ſenators preſent, treaties ſhall be formed
rationale: The paragraph restates the treaty and appointment clause of Article II, Section 2, Clause 2: "two thirds of the senators present" for treaties, and ambassadors, public ministers, consuls, judges of the supreme court and other officers appointed with the senate's consent.
to_quote: two thirds of the Senators present concur

from_quote: "The ſenate ſhall have the ſole power to try all impeachments."
rationale: The paragraph quotes in quotation marks the first sentence of Article I, Section 3, Clause 6.
to_quote: The Senate shall have the sole Power to try all Impeachments.

from_quote: adding the equal vote of the ſenate to the number each ſtate hath in the houſe of repreſentatives
rationale: The paragraph describes the electors as the senators added to the number each state has in the house of representatives, which is the apportionment of electors in Article II, Section 1, Clause 2.
to_quote: equal to the whole Number of Senators and Representatives

from_quote: Thoſe having the five higheſt votes are to be ballotted for by the houſe of repreſentatives, the vote to be taken by ſtates
rationale: The paragraph describes the choice of the president from the five highest by the house of representatives, voting by states, which is in Article II, Section 1, Clause 3.
to_quote: from the five highest on the List the said House shall in like Manner chuse the President

from_quote: That of adjournment in caſe of impeachment, between the two branches, to ſuch time as he ſhall think fit
rationale: The paragraph objects to a power of adjournment "between the two branches, to such time as he shall think fit," which echoes the president's power in Article II, Section 3 to adjourn the houses "to such Time as he shall think proper." The paragraph's words are "in case of impeachment," where the clause says in case of disagreement between the houses.
to_quote: he may adjourn them to such Time as he shall think proper

from_quote: From the firſt clauſe reſpecting the judiciary it is obvious, that the Congreſs, although there ſhall be one Supreme Court only, may eſtabliſh as many ſubordinate to it, as they ſhall think fit
rationale: The paragraph discusses "the first clause respecting the judiciary," under which congress may establish courts subordinate to the one supreme court, which is Article III, Section 1.
to_quote: in such inferior Courts as the Congress may from time to time ordain and establish

from_quote: the cognizance of all caſes ariſing under the conſtitution and the laws, either of a civil or criminal nature, in law or equity
rationale: The paragraph describes the jurisdiction of the federal courts over "all cases arising under the constitution and the laws ... in law or equity" and between citizens of the same state, which is the list of cases in Article III, Section 2, Clause 1.
to_quote: in Law and Equity, arising under this Constitution

from_quote: The appeal as to fact is ſtill more extraordinary and exceptionable
rationale: The paragraph objects to "the appeal as to fact," which refers to the supreme court's appellate jurisdiction "both as to Law and Fact" in Article III, Section 2, Clause 2.
to_quote: both as to Law and Fact

from_quote: the exerciſe of direct taxation and exciſe, by one body, over the very extenſive territory contained within the bounds of the United States
rationale: The paragraph repeats the objection to "direct taxation and excise" by the congress, the taxing power of Article I, Section 8, Clause 1.
to_quote: To lay and collect Taxes, Duties, Imposts and Excises
